about.description:
A minimal, secure Python interpreter written in Rust for use by AI.
Monty avoids the cost, latency, complexity and general faff of using full container based sandbox for running LLM generated code.
Instead, it let's you run safely run Python code written by an LLM embedded in your agent, with startup times measured in single digit microseconds not hundreds of milliseconds.
about.summary: A minimal, secure Python interpreter written in Rust for use by AI

raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "0.0.23"

recipe:
  name: pydantic-monty
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/p/pydantic-monty/pydantic_monty-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: ee674b81ed12f81cfbe0db210fe5e803c754d0682634331931f4d70d5742058d
    target_directory: pydantic-monty
  - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/p/pydantic-monty-client/pydantic_monty_client-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 8b31f75afebb60c0416c869c8d6667a75e84b0f05b7a0b44e51b77ef98f294d7
    target_directory: pydantic-monty-client
  - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/p/pydantic-monty-runtime/pydantic_monty_runtime-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: d181f557cd3d19ee826459dea234a2b440e2b6de093e66384629843959146071
    target_directory: pydantic-monty-runtime
  - url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pydantic/monty/refs/tags/v${{ version }}/LICENSE
    sha256: 5841db47ee6e1f0becafe2d19ca43c08cbc6d2c0952822ccf88cbbf2bd0749bd

build:
  number: 2

outputs:
  # The `monty` binary (maturin `bindings = "bin"`), so the wheel carries no
  # extension module and one build serves every python version.
  - package:
      name: pydantic-monty-runtime
    build:
      skip: not is_python_min
      python:
        version_independent: true
      script:
        env:
          CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP: symbols
          CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO: fat
          CARGO: cargo-auditable-wrapper${{ '' if unix else '.bat' }}
        content:
          - cd pydantic-monty-runtime
          - if: unix
            then:
              - cp ${RECIPE_DIR}/cargo-auditable-wrapper.sh ${BUILD_PREFIX}/bin/cargo-auditable-wrapper
            else:
              - copy %RECIPE_DIR%\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat %BUILD_PREFIX%\Library\bin\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat
          # cc-rs concatenates $CFLAGS with the target-scoped flags instead of
          # letting the latter win, so the cross flags leak into the build-script
          # (i.e. build platform) compilations of C crates such as `zstd-sys`
          # pulled in by `ty_vendored`. Scope them to the target instead.
          - if: build_platform != target_platform
            then:
              - export TARGET_CFLAGS="${CFLAGS}"
              - export TARGET_CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS}"
              - unset CFLAGS CXXFLAGS
          # rust-lld cannot handle some of the relocations gcc emits for ppc64le
          # (the inline-PLT R_PPC64_PLTSEQ/PLTCALL sequences), which breaks linking
          # of the C crates. gcc honours the last `-fuse-ld`, so this overrides
          # rustc's bundled rust-lld with the GNU bfd linker.
          - if: target_platform == "linux-ppc64le"
            then: export CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS="${CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS:-} -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=bfd"
          - python -m pip install . -vv
          - cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output ./THIRD_PARTY.yml
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('rust') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cargo-bundle-licenses
        - cargo-auditable
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
            - maturin >=1.14.1,<2
      host:
        - python
        - pip
        - maturin >=1.14.1,<2
      run:
        - python
    tests:
      - python:
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
          pip_check: true
      - script:
          - monty --version
    about:
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
        - pydantic-monty-runtime/THIRD_PARTY.yml

  # The `pydantic_monty` module. pyo3 without abi3, so this is built once per
  # python version.
  - package:
      name: pydantic-monty-client
    build:
      script:
        env:
          CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP: symbols
          CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO: fat
          CARGO: cargo-auditable-wrapper${{ '' if unix else '.bat' }}
        content:
          - cd pydantic-monty-client
          - if: unix
            then:
              - cp ${RECIPE_DIR}/cargo-auditable-wrapper.sh ${BUILD_PREFIX}/bin/cargo-auditable-wrapper
            else:
              - copy %RECIPE_DIR%\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat %BUILD_PREFIX%\Library\bin\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat
          # See the comment on the runtime output.
          - if: build_platform != target_platform
            then:
              - export TARGET_CFLAGS="${CFLAGS}"
              - export TARGET_CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS}"
              - unset CFLAGS CXXFLAGS
          # See the comment on the runtime output.
          - if: target_platform == "linux-ppc64le"
            then: export CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS="${CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS:-} -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=bfd"
          # `aws-lc-sys`' cc-based builder hands its ARM64 assembly to cl.exe, which
          # silently drops the `.S` files and then fails on the C feature probes.
          # Build it through CMake with clang-cl instead, and keep CMake's object
          # paths short enough for Windows.
          - if: target_platform == "win-arm64"
            then:
              - set "CARGO_TARGET_DIR=%TMP%\pydantic-monty-cargo-target"
              - set "CARGO_HOME=%TMP%\pydantic-monty-cargo-home"
              - set "AWS_LC_SYS_CMAKE_BUILDER=1"
              - set "CC_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc=clang-cl.exe"
              - set "CXX_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc=clang-cl.exe"
              - set "ASM_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc=clang-cl.exe"
              - set "CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja"
          - python -m pip install . -vv
          - cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output ./THIRD_PARTY.yml
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('rust') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cargo-bundle-licenses
        - cargo-auditable
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
            - maturin >=1.9.4,<2
        - if: target_platform == "win-arm64"
          then:
            - cmake
            - ninja
      host:
        - python
        - pip
        - maturin >=1.9.4,<2
      run:
        - python
        - typing_extensions >=4.5
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - pydantic_monty
          pip_check: true
    about:
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
        - pydantic-monty-client/THIRD_PARTY.yml

  # Metapackage pairing the module with the binary it spawns as a worker.
  - package:
      name: pydantic-monty
    build:
      skip: not (target_platform == "linux-64" and is_python_min)
      noarch: python
      python:
        entry_points:
          - pydantic-monty = pydantic_monty._cli:main
      script:
        - cd pydantic-monty
        - python -m pip install . -vv
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - hatchling
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('pydantic-monty-client', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('pydantic-monty-runtime', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - pydantic_monty
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
          pip_check: true
      # `pydantic-monty` resolves the `monty` binary from the runtime, so this
      # only passes if both halves are wired up.
      - script:
          - monty --version
          - pydantic-monty --version

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/pydantic/monty
  summary: A minimal, secure Python interpreter written in Rust for use by AI
  description: |
    A minimal, secure Python interpreter written in Rust for use by AI.
    Monty avoids the cost, latency, complexity and general faff of using full container based sandbox for running LLM generated code.
    Instead, it let's you run safely run Python code written by an LLM embedded in your agent, with startup times measured in single digit microseconds not hundreds of milliseconds.
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
  repository: https://github.com/pydantic/monty

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - pavelzw
